ai_compute_composite.cfc_nos_split_note: The central CFC/NOS split is an artefact of the cap: every 334 detail industry inherits 334's 2017 FA/GDP-by-industry ratio (1.172, capped at 1), so nearly all of its GOS becomes CFC (334111 NOS 0.016, 334413 0.041). The composite's NOS therefore understates rents in the chain where IP and institutional rents are largest (semiconductors, AI) and is not a bound on sigma; the economy-wide-ratio variant (cfc_tot_economywide, nos_tot_economywide) sits beside. The composite also weights asset-basis thetas by annual-cost shares, which leaves out the return on the hardware.

model_vs_data.note: multiple = data / model on the stated basis; like_for_like False marks a mixed-basis figure kept only because earlier prose quoted it. like_for_like is about the basis, not the scope: each row names its data scope
model_vs_data.scope_note: The chain share depends heavily on scope (2023, tot: the set 0.0591, equipment + IPP 0.1493, (c)'s bundle 0.1828). The (a)/(b) model's machine chain stands for all produced capital ((b)'s capital stock is 2.98x income, set against all fixed capital, housing structures inside it), so of the three the widest, (c)'s bundle, is the nearest match, and it still leaves out residential investment; the set and equipment + IPP rows show how much of the multiple is scope.

targets_for_macro.g1_equipment_ipp_structures_scope: Exactly the bundle calibration (c) reads (economy[year]['inv_equipment_ipp_structures_theta_tot']): fixed investment in equipment and IPP, private (F02E, F02N) and government (F06E, F06N, F07E, F07N, F10E, F10N), plus private nonresidential structures (F02S), all commodities, each commodity's sum clipped at 0. On each basis theta (compensation) + cfc + tax + nos + imports (imported content) = 1: tot prices imports at US cost shares (imports 0); dom counts imported intermediates; domp adds the imported share of the final products. sigma_upper_closed = NOS, sigma_upper_open = NOS + imported content; the multiplier bounds are 1 + theta/sigma at those bounds and 1/(1 - theta) for any sigma. Means are of the annual values. Import convention (dom, domp): the domestic share phi = q/(q + M), imports' share of total supply (the lambda thread's, gated to its series); the domestic-use convention of BEA's import matrices, 1 - M/(q + M - X), gives in 2023 theta_domp 0.4594 (against 0.4700), chain compensation share domp 0.1477 (0.1511), NOS domp 0.1893 (0.1935), imported content domp 0.2048 (0.1846), open multiplier bound 2.17 (2.24), floor 1.85 (1.89); tot is unchanged (g1_*_import_convention_domestic_use). Hours: hours_share_of_total_hours_bridged_* borrows the medium (machinery) set's FTE-to-hours-worked bridge (0.904 in 2023), untested for the bundle's mix (R&D and professional services, computer services, construction, trade), so the FTE and bridged shares are a range, not a point (g1_*_hours_share_range_2023).

notes.set_label: The 'machinery + software set (investment-weighted)' (keyed 'machinery_software_set'; formerly 'all machinery') is six commodities (333, 334, 335, 511, 514, 5415; 532RL carries no investment), 37% of equipment + IPP investment in 2023. It leaves out vehicles, aircraft, R&D (5412OP's F02N), furniture and the trade margins on equipment (weights at producers' prices), and it includes government equipment, defense among it. Its 2023 theta_tot 0.617 is the top of a 0.546-0.617 range across scopes (range_2023_tot_across_scopes).

cfc_cap_and_fallback.summary: Where FA's CFC exceeds GDP-by-industry GOS the ratio is capped at 1 (central); where GOS is not positive, CFC per $ of gross output is used (fallback). It is not only R&D in 334: 5415 carries 22%-24% of the set's weight in those years (29%-36% in 2015-2023) and is capped in 1999, 2001-2007 and on the fallback in 2000, so the set's 1999-2007 cost split is shaped by it. The cap removes at most 0.0526 of $1 of the set's final output in any year (0.0257 in 2015-2023) and at most 0.0200 of the (c) bundle's (0.0105 in 2015-2023); each removal is (ratio - 1) x the industry's GOS along the chain, per $1 of final output (tot). Exercised stock options in NIPA compensation also depress tech GOS around 2000 (stock_options).

notes.stock_options: NIPA compensation includes exercised employee stock options (recorded in wages and salaries at exercise). In the tech industries (511, 514, 5415) part of that is a claim on rents, and around 2000 it depresses measured GOS: GDP-by-industry GOS of 5415 was -3,101 $m in 2000 and of 514 -1,729 / -17,169 / -1,785 $m in 1999-2001, which puts them on the per-output CFC fallback, and 514's theta_tot reaches 1.002 in 2000. The dot-com bust's losses and the option exercises are not separated here.
notes.ai_composite: The central CFC/NOS split is an artefact of the cap: every 334 detail industry inherits 334's 2017 FA/GDP-by-industry ratio (1.172, capped at 1), so nearly all of its GOS becomes CFC (334111 NOS 0.016, 334413 0.041). The composite's NOS therefore understates rents in the chain where IP and institutional rents are largest (semiconductors, AI) and is not a bound on sigma; the economy-wide-ratio variant (cfc_tot_economywide, nos_tot_economywide) sits beside. The composite also weights asset-basis thetas by annual-cost shares, which leaves out the return on the hardware. Economy-wide-ratio variant: CFC 0.208, NOS 0.307 (central CFC 0.395, NOS 0.120).
notes.service_conversion: (i) The user cost is (rho + delta) V, with no term for the asset's relative price change. ICT and software prices fall against the GDP price index (mean 2015-2023: 334 -0.040, 511 -0.046, 514 -0.042, 5415 -0.040, 333 -0.002 a year), which raises their user cost and lowers the service share: with it the set's 2023 service share is 0.456 against 0.488 central (-3.3 points; service_relative_price_variant). (ii) The service share depends on delta: the set's 2023 delta is 0.218, calibration (b)'s 0.08; at (b)'s delta the same theta 0.617 gives 0.359, not 0.488. The service share is therefore not a free-standing target: theta_V and delta are targeted jointly (macro.calibrate_c does). (iii) The conversion is steady-state and one-sector: during a build-out, investment exceeds replacement.
notes.per_income: (i) The relative basis gives every percentile the economy-wide compensation/wage ratio (1.213 in 2023). Benefit loads are lower at low wages, so P10's compensation per hour, and with it P10's chain hours per hour replaced, is overstated (an upward bias at P10, smaller or reversed toward the top). The OEWS mean in the ratio is job-weighted, not hours-weighted. (ii) The central values carry the bridge to the lambda thread's hours-worked construction (0.904 in 2023; 0.864-0.928 over 1998-2023), which rests on WIOD SEA levels to 2014 and KLEMS-index tails for 2015-23 from a KLEMS workbook (klems_ilpa_1997_2024.xlsx) with no recorded source URL; so the unbridged relative_fte values are published beside it as a co-headline (headline per_income_2023_service_relative_fte). (iii) OEWS method breaks: the 2002-03 move to May panels, SOC 2010 in 2012, SOC 2018 phased in over 2019-21, model-based estimation from May 2021, and the published top code (a wage at or above it is shown as '#'): $70 from 2001, $80 from 2008, $90 from 2011, $100 from 2016, $115 from 2022 (the May 2022 change: $100 -> $115). All-occupation P10-P90 lie far below every top code (2023 P90 $58.40), so only the mean, the relative basis's denominator, can be touched, if its top band moved with the code (not verified).
notes.rho_central: rho_central 0.0575 is imported from macro.CAPITAL_BASE.rho, not hard-coded: calibration (b)'s return, kept for comparison (the key's name predates calibration (c), whose own rho, 0.0755, is an outcome of calibrate_c reading this file's targets — circular here).
notes.io_release: The I-O tables are the lambda thread's cached release (zip members dated 2024-08-28 12:43 to 2024-09-25 18:46; data to 2023); the FA CFC and GDP-by-industry GOS behind the CFC/GOS ratios are the Sep 2026 releases, so the ratios are taken across releases and applied to the older I-O's V003 row. 2023 total GOS: I-O 11.721 $tn, TVA113 11.809 $tn (0.75% apart). pull() does not refresh the I-O while the gate is pinned to that release.
